name: Roaming Throne
oracle_text:
Ward {2}
As this creature enters, choose a creature type.
This creature is the chosen type in addition to its other types.
If a triggered ability of another creature you control of the chosen type triggers, it triggers an additional time.
blocked_sentences: This creature is the chosen type in addition to its other types.

needs.what: `{"chosen_type_of": "self"}` accepted on the GRANT side of a subtype-changing effect, not only on the filter side -- i.e. `{"kind": "static", "effect": "add_subtype", "affects": {"self_only": true}, "subtypes": [{"chosen_type_of": "self"}]}` loading and layering the type the source actually chose. Three places have to change together: `AbilityModel.subtypes` (src/automtg/cards/schema.py:524) must accept the mapping entry beside plain strings the way a filter's `subtypes` already does; the layer-4 loop in `characteristics._derived_characteristics` (src/automtg/engine/characteristics.py:299-303), which today does a bare `subtypes.update(static.get("subtypes", ()))`, must resolve the entry against `source_obj.chosen_type` (and add nothing while no type has been chosen, matching `resolve_chosen_subtypes`' "\u0000none" convention for the filter side); and `ops_characteristics.op_add_subtype` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_characteristics.py:44) must do the same substitution rather than `str()`. It is the Arcane Adaptation / Xenograft / Conspiracy family as well as this card, and it must be a continuous grant so the type is re-read after a `change_text` or a second `choose_type`.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `chosen_type_of` exists but is a **read**, not a grant: `characteristics.resolve_chosen_subtypes` (src/automtg/engine/characteristics.py:1192) rewrites a *selector's* `subtypes`, and its only callers are filter matchers -- `_matches` (line 1390), `triggers` line 1338, `player_statics` lines 670/1044, `selectors.py` line 610. Every shipped user of it (Vanquisher's Banner, Cavern of Souls, Urza's Incubator, Coat of Arms-style anthems) asks "is this other object of the chosen type"; none makes its own source *be* that type, and this card needs the second thing. The static `add_subtype` is the right effect and refuses the entry outright -- `compile_card` on `{"effect": "add_subtype", "affects": {"self_only": true}, "subtypes": [{"chosen_type_of": "self"}]}` fails pydantic validation with `abilities.0.subtypes.0: Input should be a valid string`, because `AbilityModel.subtypes` is `list[str]`. The `add_subtype` OP is the trap, and it is why this is a gap rather than a near miss: the same spec inside a `self_enters` trigger *compiles clean*, then `op_add_subtype` does `subtypes = [str(t) for t in spec.get("subtypes", ())]`, so the permanent gains the literal subtype string `"{'chosen_type_of': 'self'}"` -- a card that loads, resolves, passes a zone assertion and is of no creature type at all. `animate` and the `set_types` static are no substitute twice over: their subtype lists are literal `list[str]` on the same model and they *replace* the type line, while the printed words are "in addition to its other types". Nothing else reaches a permanent's own chosen type: `value_keys` has no chosen-type leaf, `change_text` rewrites printed names rather than adding one, and `grant_ability` grants abilities, not types. The card's other three sentences are all expressible and verified to compile -- `ward` as a `{"affects": {"self_only": true}, "cost": {"mana": "{2}"}}` static, the choice as a `self_enters` trigger holding `choose_type`, and the doubler as a `double_triggers` static whose `affects` is `{"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "exclude_self": true, "subtypes": [{"chosen_type_of": "self"}]}` -- so this one line is the whole of the work.
